observed_result:
12 top-level tests pass, 0 fail, under -race on go1.26.5 darwin/arm64 (ok, 1.474s). The trainable controller meets its acceptance: the gradient path and capacity are inspectable, there is no target bypass, and a capacity-matched control exists.

Controller forward pass by hand (TestControllerHandForward): with Nodes 2, Hidden 1, a window of two rows, no feedback and no resources, W1={1,0}, b1={0}, w2={1}, b2={0}, the first release over window rows {0,0} and {1,1} reads mean 0.5 and population variance 0.25 (Nodes x window = 4 values) and releases softplus(tanh(0.5)) on channel 1 while channel 0 stays exactly 0 (Channels = Channel+1 = 2); the second release over the window {1,1} twice reads mean 1 and variance 0 and releases softplus(tanh(1)); channel 0 stays 0. An activity row of the wrong width is refused, and a nil activity is the declared Nodes as zeros rather than a refusal.

Feedback and resources enter the input (TestControllerReadsFeedbackAndResources): InputWidth is 4 for summary mean + variance + feedback score + one resource; with x = {4, 0, 0.5, 2} (window row {4} for mean 4 and variance 0, feedback score 0.5, energy 2) the release is softplus(tanh(0.5+2)); with the resource missing the release is softplus(tanh(0.5)), so an absent declared resource reads zero and is not a refusal; with no feedback the release is softplus(tanh(2)); feedback that has not yet arrived is refused.

Capacity counts (TestControllerValidateAndCounts): for Hidden 3 and InputWidth 4 the parameter count is 19 = 3*4 + 3 + 3 + 1 and the per-step mult-adds are 15 = 3*4 + 3; Channels is 1; all eleven broken declarations (too few/too many parameters, no or too long window, duplicate or blank resource, no node, no or too many hidden units, negative channel, non-finite parameter) are refused by both Validate and Release.

SourceSpec builds a controller (TestSourceSpecBuildsAController): Build returns a *Controller declaring Channels 2; the built source owns its buffers, so writing into the spec after the build does not change the released value softplus(tanh(0.5)); five ambiguous or mismatched specs (different channel, no body, another kind's body, two bodies, invalid body) are refused.

No target bypass, both halves: TestControllerHasNoTargetField reflects Controller, ControllerInputs and SourceContext and refuses any field whose name contains "target"; scripts/check-target-flow.sh then prints PASS for dynamics, simulate, modulation and plasticity (no signal.Target and no NewTarget( in non-test files; file counts 10, 11, 10 and 1 respectively), PASS for learning (no type, 18 non-test files), and PASS that dynamics, simulate, modulation and plasticity each have no dependency on the learning package, ending with 'RESULT: a target reaches no forward or modulation package (SIG-03 compile-time check passed)' and exit 0.

Controller gradient against finite differences (TestControllerGradientMatchesFiniteDifferences): for each of the 25 parameters of the fixture (Nodes 3, Hidden 4, InputWidth 4 = activity mean, activity variance, feedback score, energy, window 2, parameter order row-major W1 then b1 then w2 then b2), the analytic gradient of (release - proxy)^2 is compared with a central difference (eps 1e-6) of the hand-replayed loss; worst relative error 4.919340696604421e-09 for the reward proxy (proxy = feedback input 0.3) and 6.235998255320076e-09 for the activity target (proxy = max(0, 0.7 - mean activity)), well under the 1e-5 bound. TestControllerGradientRejects refuses a controller with no release yet, the reward proxy on a controller that does not read feedback, an unknown or empty objective kind, a non-finite target, and updates with a wrong-length gradient or a loose rate, leaving the parameters untouched.

Update descends the objective (TestControllerUpdateReducesLoss): 20 passes of Release, Gradient and Update(rate 0.05) keep the loss non-increasing step to step (refusing any rise beyond 1e-12) and take it from 0.9084832839974664 after the first pass to 0.010770769812422113 after 19 updates, still below the first value; Update returns a copy, and writing into it does not move the controller's parameters.

Capacity-matched control (TestCapacityMatchedHasEqualParameterCount): NewCapacityMatched builds a MemoryController with the same InputWidth 4, the same ParameterCount 19 and the same MultAddsPerStep 15 as the source controller, with its own copies of the parameter and resource slices. Its forward pass is the controller's with the softplus taken off (TestMemoryControllerHandForward): the same parameters {1,0,0,2,0.5} on the window row {1,1} (mean 1, variance 0) give the linear offset 2*tanh(1) + 0.5, and the release the controller produces for the same inputs is softplus of exactly that number. Its gradient matches finite differences (TestMemoryControllerGradientMatchesFiniteDifferences): over the 19 parameters of the fixture (Nodes 3, Hidden 3, InputWidth 4, window 2), the analytic gradient of (offset - 0.2)^2 against a central difference of the hand-replayed loss has worst relative error 3.358017227354867e-09. TestMemoryControllerValidateRejects refuses a short parameter vector, zero hidden units, NewCapacityMatched(nil), and a gradient before any Offset.
assumption_statement: The controller gradient is computed, per the ticket's gradient-path decision, only through the controller's own output against a declared objective (reward_proxy or activity_target); both proxies are read from the very inputs the release read, so their derivatives with respect to every parameter are zero and the gradient never crosses concentration, receptors or the core, whose differentiable path is a separate requirement when it is opened. The capacity-matched control's output is added directly to the readout, and its own learning target is the residual the readout leaves, never a release. The window and the cached forward pass a Controller or MemoryController carries across Release/Offset calls are state, not declaration, and are not part of any snapshot in this stage: a restored controller starts its window from zeros again. The two objectives are the only declared proxies; there is no target field anywhere, and a target reaches the controller only as a number the caller hands to Gradient's objective.
limitations: The window state is not part of any snapshot in this stage; a restored controller restarts its window from zeros (documented in modulation/controller.go and memory_controller.go, asserted by construction rather than by a snapshot round-trip test).
Only two objective proxies exist (reward_proxy and activity_target), and the controller can train only against declared objectives; real teacher or natural-reward targets are outside this ticket.
No real-data or whole-brain run; all numbers come from the code-declared fixtures (three neurons at most) on one machine.

The gradient is checked against finite differences of the fixtures' own hand-replayed losses, not on a trained task, and only for the tanh/softplus MLP shape; the concentration -> receptor -> core differentiable path is explicitly not implemented.

The recorded log contains only the twelve tests the -run pattern selected; the shared-source tests of sources_test.go (feedback arrival, non-negative releases for every source) and the full go test ./... and go vet ./... runs are outside this command's scope.
